name: Psychological Detachment
summary: Mentally switching off from work during non-work time, which is one of the strongest predictors of recovery from job stress.
explanation:
Psychological detachment means leaving work mentally as well as physically. During your evening, weekend or holiday, you don't think about tasks, answer messages or replay problems.

Sabine Sonnentag and Charlotte Fritz made detachment one of four recovery experiences, next to relaxation, mastery and control. Across many diary and longitudinal studies, people who detach more report less exhaustion, better sleep, better mood and more engagement the next day. Their stressor-detachment model adds a nasty trap. High job demands make detachment harder exactly when you need it most, so stress and poor recovery feed each other.

Detachment is attention residue at the scale of the workday. Unfinished tasks and open loops follow you home and keep the work mind running. What helps? A shutdown ritual that captures open loops and writes down the next steps for tomorrow is a good start. So are physical or digital boundaries (e.g., no work apps on your personal phone), and absorbing non-work activities such as sport, music or social time, which leave no room for work thoughts.

Don't confuse detachment with disengagement. You can care a lot about your work during work hours. Detachment is about letting your mind fully leave it afterwards, so that it comes back rested.
